exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I usually buy Good Culture, but it is unavailable. What should I buy instead, and why?
reviewed_answer:
Buy Daisy 4% Small Curd Cottage Cheese as your closest everyday substitute. In a blind taste test, Daisy ranked best overall for its soft, evenly formed curds and rich creaminess; it also has a very short ingredient list—skim milk, cultured cream, and salt—so it most closely matches Good Culture’s clean-label appeal.

Best substitutes by priority
If you want…	Buy	Why
Closest all-purpose replacement	Daisy 4% Small Curd	Creamy, plush curds and simple ingredients; best for eating straight, with fruit, or as a dip. 

Lower fat, similar protein	Daisy 2% Low Fat	Explicitly recommended as a Good Culture alternative; Good Culture’s 2% version has about 14 g protein per half-cup, so compare labels for your preferred macro profile. 

Organic / cleaner ingredient list	Organic Valley	Named a runner-up for balanced curds and creaminess, and chefs also recommend it as a Good Culture alternative. 

Blending into smoothies, sauces, or egg bites	365 Organic (Whole Foods)	Its small, soft curds blend especially smoothly. 

Cooking, such as gnocchi, kugel, or stuffed shells	Breakstone’s	Smaller curds and a slightly drier texture help it integrate without making dishes watery. 
What to look for

Since you like Good Culture, prioritize:

Small curd rather than large curd for a closer texture.

2% or 4% milkfat depending on whether you usually buy the low-fat or classic version.

Live and active cultures if you value the tangy flavor and probiotic aspect.

A short ingredient list and minimal gums/stabilizers, which are part of Good Culture’s appeal.

If you can only find one: Daisy. If your usual Good Culture is the 2% low-fat tub, choose Daisy 2% Low Fat first; if it is the 4% classic, choose Daisy 4% Small Curd.
